title: Deterministic Verification and a Single‑Repair Guardrail for LLM‑Generated Network Configurations: A Paired, Shared‑Candidate Study
abstract: We report a sealed, preregistered paired experiment that measured the marginal verifier-detected effect of interposing a deterministic validator plus at most one automated repair on the same LLM-generated configuration candidate. Under the preregistered shared_initial_candidate semantics (exactly one initial generation call per intent; that same candidate reused for both baseline and guarded episodes) we generated one candidate per natural-language intent with gpt-5-mini for N = 250 pairs and evaluated two episodes per intent: baseline (accept candidate) and guarded (deterministic validator; if failing, permit one automated repair). Execution completed 500 episodes with model_calls_used = 251. Results: baseline verifier-pass 249/250 (99.6%), guarded verifier-pass 250/250 (100.0%); contingency n11 = 249, n10 = 1, n01 = 0, n00 = 0; paired difference (guarded − baseline) = +0.4 percentage points, 95% CI [0.0, 1.2 pp] (paired bootstrap percentile, 10,000 resamples, seed = 1729), exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0. The single discordant pair was converted to pass by the single permitted repair. All execution and analysis artifacts are archived in the registered evidence bundle referenced in the Disclosure Statement.

sections.introduction:
Generative large language models (LLMs) are being explored as intent-to-configuration translators in network operations (NetOps), promising faster authoring of device CLI sequences and intent-driven automation. Stochastic generation, however, creates operational risk: syntax errors, incorrect command ordering, local-policy violations, and vendor-CLI subtleties can produce unsafe or non-functional device changes. Prior empirical and survey work documents LLM feasibility for draft configurations while highlighting the continuing need for deterministic verification or human oversight [1], [2].

A widely adopted architectural response is to interpose a deterministic validator between generation and acceptance, optionally followed by bounded automated repair — a generate–verify–repair (GVR) pattern — which accepts only validator-passed candidates or attempts limited repair when mechanically verifiable defects are detected [3], [4]. These pipelines reduce mechanically verifiable error classes (syntax, ordering, and local-policy violations), but open questions remain about the marginal benefit of such guardrails when modern LLM outputs already conform to validator encodings under constrained task regimes.

This paper reports a preregistered, artifact-backed paired experiment that isolates the marginal verifier+single-repair effect when the same initial candidate is reused across conditions (shared_initial_candidate semantics). By design the experiment measures only the validator-and-repair marginal effect on identical model outputs rather than conflating generation variability across conditions. We executed N_pairs = 250 constrained intent tasks in a synthetic/emulation partition and report concrete, artifact-grounded quantification of the marginal verifier-detected improvement under these conditions.
sections.related_work:
Empirical and survey studies of LLMs in NetOps and related code/configuration domains motivate guarded pipelines and verifier-driven repair. Representative NetOps evaluations show that LLMs can produce usable draft configurations for constrained intents but often require downstream checks for safety and correctness [1], [2]. Work on self-correction and LLM-native repair highlights that LLMs alone are unreliable for eliminating all classes of errors without dependable external feedback or mechanical checks [2], [6].

Formal and tool-based verification approaches (header-space analysis, Batfish-style checks and localized model checking) provide mature, deterministic checks for many mechanically verifiable errors; these tools are natural validators in GVR architectures and have been used to detect ordering, syntax, and reachability defects in generated artifacts [4], [5]. Program-repair and generate-and-validate lines of work show that constrained, verifier-guided repair can convert many verifier-detected failures into passes in code and configuration contexts, though success depends on defect class and repair template expressivity [3], [6].

Security analyses of LLM-integrated systems document prompt-injection and indirect instruction channels as practical threats; defensive layers (filtering, detector classifiers, provenance constraints) mitigate known attacks but do not eliminate adaptive adversaries in operational settings [7].

This study differs from prior work by (i) using a preregistered paired design with shared_initial_candidate semantics that isolates the validator/repair marginal effect on identical generated candidates, (ii) reporting deterministic reconciliation of provider-call accounting and stage-level modeling for generation and repair calls, and (iii) archiving validator and repair traces so numeric outcomes and stage mappings are auditable from the evidence bundle.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and estimand. The experiment was preregistered and specified a confirmatory paired design with N_pairs = 250, generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate, and the primary estimand paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline. The preregistration froze the single-repair policy, exclusion rules, analysis tests (exact McNemar two-sided and paired-bootstrap percentile CIs), and the maximum model-call budget.

Shared_initial_candidate semantics. Under the registered shared_initial_candidate design exactly one initial model-generation call was produced per intent and that same generated candidate was reused for both episodes (baseline and guarded); no independent first-pass generation per condition was performed. This isolates the marginal effect of deterministic validation and the single permitted repair on identical candidates and creates a paired outcome per intent where differences can only arise from the deterministic validator and any allowed repair.

Task generation and constraints. A deterministic task generator produced 250 constrained intent tasks that included initial_state, expected_final_state, required_sequence, allowed_touched_fields, and a difficulty label (medium/hard/very_hard). Tasks exercised workflow constraints (for example, make-before-break uplink switchover, paired-link atomic MTU changes, and safe access transfer patterns) and enforced protected interfaces that must not be modified. The task payloads and manifest were deterministically generated and archived.

Model invocation and repair policy. The declared model for all initial generations was gpt-5-mini. For each intent we executed one shared initial generation call. The preregistration permitted up to one automated repair call per episode; execution exercised exactly one repair call in total. Provider-call reconciliation reports model_calls_used = 251 (250 initial generations + 1 repair); stage_counts recorded shared_initial_generation = 250 and repair = 1.

Guarded pipeline, deterministic validator, and repair templates. The guarded pipeline submitted the shared candidate to a deterministic network validator that (i) parses CLI sequences, (ii) counts parsed_command_count, (iii) checks required_sequence ordering, (iv) validates workflow constraints (group-activity and make-before-break rules), and (v) compares the resulting final_state snapshot to the task-encoded expected_final_state. Validator outputs include normalized_configuration, parsed_command_count, required_command_count, observed_touched_field_count, violation_codes, and a boolean valid flag.

When the validator returned valid = false in the guarded episode, the pipeline permitted one automated, template-driven repair attempt constrained to deterministic syntactic and ordering fixes (e.g., reorder commands to match required_sequence, split or join multi-command lines, correct command-token ordering). No multi-iteration repair or human escalation was permitted by design.

Inclusion and exclusion rules. The preregistered exclusion rules removed items failing deterministic vendor-parsers that prevented verification, or items with credential-like tokens or denylist hits. In this confirmatory run no episodes were excluded or flagged and complete_pair_count = 250.

Analysis plan. The preregistered primary analysis used a paired binary executor. The primary test is an exact two-sided McNemar on paired outcomes; we also computed a paired-bootstrap percentile 95% CI for guarded − baseline using 10,000 resamples (bootstrap_seed = 1729). The analysis executor and all analysis artifacts are archived.
sections.results:
Execution and raw counts. Execution completed the confirmatory partition with planned_episode_count = 500, completed_episode_count = 500, complete_pair_count = 250, and model_calls_used = 251. Provider-call accounting reconciles to 250 shared initial-generation calls plus 1 repair call.

Primary binary outcomes and contingency. Validator-scored successes: baseline_success_count = 249 (baseline_success_rate = 0.996), guarded_success_count = 250 (guarded_success_rate = 1.0). The observed paired contingency is n11 = 249, n10 = 1, n01 = 0, n00 = 0. The single discordant pair (baseline failed, guarded passed) corresponds to the only exercised repair call; the repair-conversion rate on the confirmatory partition is 1/250 = 0.004 (0.4%).

Statistical inference and uncertainty. The exact McNemar two-sided test on discordant counts (n10 = 1, n01 = 0) returned p = 1.0. The paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI for guarded − baseline (10,000 resamples; bootstrap_seed = 1729) is [0.0, 0.012] (0 – 1.2 percentage points). These analysis outputs are archived and deterministically reproducible from the preserved analysis artifacts.

Representative diagnostics and repair. Representative validator diagnostics show parsed_command_count and required_command_count equal for passed episodes; for example, a medium-difficulty task had parsed_command_count = 4 and required_command_count = 4 with valid = true. Only one automated repair was triggered and it converted the single failing baseline candidate to a guarded pass; the repair trace and guarded scoring artifact for that pair are archived.

Missingness and exclusions. No episodes were excluded: complete_pairs = 250 and all missingness counts = 0. Contamination detectors flagged no confirmatory episodes.
sections.discussion:
Interpretation of the near-null marginal effect. Under the preregistered shared_initial_candidate semantics and the constrained synthetic/emulation partition, the marginal verifier-detected benefit of inserting a deterministic validator plus a single automated repair was small: initial gpt-5-mini candidates satisfied the deterministic validator in 249/250 cases and the guarded pipeline converted the lone failing candidate via the single permitted repair. The paired-bootstrap CI upper bound (1.2 percentage points) quantifies the maximum plausible verifier-detected improvement under this pipeline and task scope.

Why the observed gain is small (artifact-grounded). Three artifact-grounded explanations account for the small observed marginal improvement: (1) the deterministic task generator encoded constrained intents, allowed_touched_fields, and required_sequences that reduced ambiguity and favored well-formed CLI sequences; (2) the declared model (gpt-5-mini) produced highly consistent, syntactically well-formed sequences for these constrained intents; and (3) the deterministic validator checks mechanically verifiable properties (syntax, required_sequence, final_state snapshot) and does not capture live protocol-level correctness or complex cross-device interactions.

Statistical power and realized baseline rate. The preregistered power calculation assumed a baseline pass rate ≈ 0.90 when selecting N_pairs = 250 to target detection of a 15 percentage-point absolute effect with ≈80% power. The realized baseline pass rate (0.996) is substantially higher than assumed and therefore reduces power to detect small absolute improvements. Given the observed data, the paired-bootstrap CI is a more informative descriptor of uncertainty than the p-value for small absolute differences.

Operational implications and appropriate framing. These results show that in tightly constrained emulation-style tasks with a capable LLM the marginal verifier-detected improvement from a single repair may be small. This should not be taken to imply validators or repairs are unnecessary in broader or adversarial contexts: validators that check richer properties, multi-iteration repairs, human-in-the-loop escalation, production heterogeneity, or adaptive adversaries could materially change the benefit calculus.

Failure modes, diagnostic patterns, and scope. The single failing baseline candidate (converted by repair) exhibited an ordering defect detectable by the deterministic validator and correctable by a simple reorder repair template. Other failure modes that a syntactic/order-focused validator cannot detect — for example, vendor-specific semantic mismatches, emergent protocol interactions, or cross-device timing-dependent hazards — were outside the validator's scope and therefore outside this study's estimand. External validity is limited to the synthetic/emulation partition executed here; preregistered community and production-like partitions were not executed.

Reproducibility and auditability. All run artifacts (raw model responses, validator traces, repair traces, reconciliation, and analysis outputs) are archived in the evidence bundle. Key numeric reconciliation facts reported above (model_calls_used = 251; stage_counts: shared_initial_generation = 250, repair = 1; contingency counts n11 = 249, n10 = 1, n01 = 0, n00 = 0; bootstrap parameters) are reproducible from those archived manifests.
sections.conclusion: We executed a sealed, preregistered paired experiment under shared_initial_candidate semantics to measure the verifier-detected marginal benefit of deterministic validation plus one permitted automated repair on identical LLM-generated configuration candidates. In N = 250 constrained synthetic intent tasks, initial gpt-5-mini candidates passed the deterministic validator in 249/250 cases; the guarded pipeline converted the single failing candidate via the single permitted repair. Observed paired improvement = 0.4 percentage points (95% CI [0.0, 1.2 pp]; p = 1.0). The study's conclusions are explicitly bounded: they apply to the shared_initial_candidate estimand exercised on the synthetic/emulation partition with the declared model, validator, and one-repair policy. Broader production, adversarial, multi-model, and multi-iteration repair evaluations remain necessary to establish generality. The archived artifacts provide deterministic reproducibility of all reported numbers and diagnostic traces.

disclosure_statement:
Human role and autonomy boundary: After an autonomy lock required by the CNSM Agentic AI Researcher track, the autonomous system performed literature search, study selection, preregistration freeze, prompt preservation, model calls, deterministic validation, permitted repair execution, analysis, drafting, peer-review, revision, and finalization without manual human editing of technical content. A human Research Director selected the broad topic family and performed pre-lock infrastructure development only; no human manually edited manuscript technical content after the autonomy lock.

Models and tools: declared model = gpt-5-mini; deterministic validator = deterministic_netops_validator_v5; deterministic task generator = deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5; adapter family = hosted_netops_gvr_v1. Execution used a guarded generate–verify–repair flow permitting at most one automated repair per episode. Provider-call accounting reconciles to model_calls_used = 251 (250 shared initial_generation + 1 repair) with per-stage counts recorded in the archived reconciliation artifact.

Preregistration and immutable prompt reference: the study was preregistered under study_id study-cand-2026-LLM-verifier-sim2real-v1. The immutable master prompt used to initiate the autonomous run is archived as provenance/master_prompt.txt with SHA-256 = 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba. The evidence bundle contains the archived preregistration, execution manifests, raw responses, validator traces, repair traces, and analysis artifacts referenced in this manuscript.
limitations: Confirmatory scope limited to the synthetic/emulation partition; preregistered community and production-like partitions were not executed and remain exploratory.

Deterministic validator assessed mechanically verifiable properties (syntax and prescribed workflow sequences) but did not measure broader semantic or behavioral correctness (protocol dynamics, emergent interactions).
Single declared model (gpt-5-mini) and one validator implementation were used; results do not establish multi-model or alternate-validator generality.
Only one automated repair attempt was permitted by design; multi-iteration repairs or human-in-the-loop escalation were not evaluated.
Adversarial and retrieval-based attacks (adaptive prompt-injection, vendor-targeted exploit vectors) and large-scale production heterogeneity were not exercised and remain open threats.
